season.short_description: Season the weekly count belongs to, e.g. 2024-25.
season.long_description: Respiratory virus season the count belongs to, written as the two calendar years it spans. Flu counts restart each August; RSV cumulative counts carry doses given since August 2023 even though only the current season's weeks are published.

vaccine.short_description: flu (seasonal influenza vaccine, adults 18+) or rsv (RSV vaccine, adults 50+).
vaccine.long_description: Vaccine the count refers to. flu = seasonal influenza vaccine doses given to adults 18 and older (2019-20 season onward). rsv = RSV vaccine doses (Arexvy, Abrysvo, or mResvia) given to adults 50 and older regardless of risk status, because the claims data cannot identify high-risk conditions.

setting.long_name: Setting where the vaccine was administered
setting.short_description: Pharmacy, Physician Medical Office, or Combined (the two together).
setting.long_description: Setting where the doses were administered: Pharmacy (retail chain, mass merchandise, food store, and independent pharmacies, from IQVIA prescription claims), Physician Medical Office (offices of physicians on the American Medical Association list, from IQVIA medical claims), or Combined (the sum of the two). Workplaces, community sites, long-term care, public health clinics, and hospitals are not represented.

age.long_description: Age group of the people vaccinated. Flu counts are reported for adults 18+, 18-49, 18-64, 50-64, 65+, and since the 2023-24 season 60-74 and 75+; RSV counts for 50-59, 60-74, and 75+. IQVIA assigns age from year of birth only, so people are treated as born on January 1.

iqvia_doses.long_name: Estimated vaccine doses administered during the week
iqvia_doses.short_description: Estimated number of doses given in the setting during the week ending on the date.
iqvia_doses.long_description: CDC's estimate of the number of vaccine doses administered in the setting during the week, projected by IQVIA from a sample of pharmacies (prescription claims, through Friday of the week) and physician offices (medical claims, through Saturday of the week) to all such settings nationally. Estimates include doses billed to insurers and paid in cash. Pharmacy estimates are revised for 13 weeks and physician office estimates can rise by up to about 10 percent as claims mature. These are counts of doses, not coverage, and cannot be turned into a percent vaccinated.
iqvia_doses.statement: About {value} doses were administered in pharmacies and physician offices in the week ending {time}

iqvia_cumulative_doses.short_description: Estimated doses given in the setting from the start of the season (flu) or since August 2023 (RSV) through the week.
iqvia_cumulative_doses.long_description: Running total of iqvia_doses from the start of the flu season (August) through the week for flu, or since August 12, 2023 for RSV, in the setting and age group. RSV totals published for the 2025-26 season therefore start above 15 million doses for adults 60 and older. National only; counts of doses, not coverage.

iqvia.name: IQVIA pharmacy and physician-office vaccination claims (CDC estimates)
iqvia.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, using IQVIA data
iqvia.location: Weekly Cumulative Estimated Number of Influenza (and RSV) Vaccinations Administered in Retail Pharmacies and Physicians' Medical Offices, Adults, United States (FluVaxView and RSVVaxView dashboards)
iqvia.description: CDC publishes weekly estimates of the number of influenza (adults 18 and older, 2019-20 season onward) and RSV (adults 50 and older) vaccine doses administered in retail pharmacies and physicians' medical offices in the United States. The pharmacy estimates are projected by IQVIA from its Longitudinal Prescription Claims (LRx) data covering about 41,000 of the roughly 57,000 U.S. retail pharmacies; the physician-office estimates are projected from IQVIA Medical Claims (Dx) for a subset of office-based physicians on the American Medical Association list. Doses given at workplaces, community sites, long-term care facilities, public health clinics, and hospitals are not captured, and the estimates are national dose counts with no denominator, so CDC states they must not be used to calculate vaccination coverage. Physician-office estimates continue to rise for about two months as claims are processed. IQVIA assigns age from year of birth. Each RSV season is published under a new dataset ID (52ds-xw49 for 2025-26).
iqvia.restrictions: Public domain as published by CDC on data.cdc.gov. The estimates are CDC projections derived from proprietary IQVIA pharmacy and physician-office claims data; reuse should attribute them to CDC FluVaxView/RSVVaxView and note that they are based on IQVIA data.

_catalog.summary: CDC's weekly estimates of how many flu and RSV vaccine doses adults received at retail pharmacies and doctors' offices nationwide, based on IQVIA claims data.

files.data.csv.gz: Weekly national dose counts by vaccine, setting, and age group
